[![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-stable-blue.svg)](https://MakieOrg.github.io/MakieTeX.jl/stable/)
[![Dev](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-dev-blue.svg)](https://MakieOrg.github.io/MakieTeX.jl/dev/)
[![Build Status](https://github.com/MakieOrg/MakieTeX.jl/actions/workflows/CI.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/MakieOrg/MakieTeX.jl/actions/workflows/CI.yml?query=branch%3Amaster)

MakieTeX plugs into [Makie](https://docs.makie.org/)'s `text` recipe via a `text_handler` attribute. Drop in a real engine — LaTeX or Typst — for individual text elements (titles, axis labels, annotations), or route every string through the engine so fonts match across the figure. It also provides `MakieTeX.PDF` and `MakieTeX.SVG` types for using vector assets as scatter markers.

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| echo: false
using CairoMakie, MakieTeX, tectonic_jll
const FONT = joinpath(Makie.assetpath(), "fonts", "TeXGyreHerosMakie-Regular.otf")
set_theme!(fonts = (regular = FONT, bold = FONT, italic = FONT, bold_italic = FONT))
const ASSETS = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "docs", "src", "assets")
```

## Install

```julia
import Pkg
Pkg.add("MakieTeX")
```

Enable an engine via package extension:

- **LaTeX** — `import tectonic_jll` (bundled, no local TeX install needed) or have `latexmk` on `PATH`.
- **Typst** — `import Typstry` (bundles the Typst compiler).

## Real LaTeX in titles, axis labels, and layout cells

Pass a `MakieTeX.LaTeX()` handler via `set_theme!`, `with_theme(...) do ... end`, or as a per-plot `text_handler` keyword. Any `L"…"` content then routes through the LaTeX engine — including documents using `tikz-feynman` and other complex packages:

```{julia}
handler = MakieTeX.LaTeX(
    render_strings = true,
    engine = `tectonic`,
    preamble = raw"""
        \usepackage{amsmath, amssymb, xcolor}
        \usepackage{tikz}
        \usepackage[compat=1.1.0]{tikz-feynman}
    """,
)

diagram = L"""
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{feynman}
  \vertex (i1) at (-2, 1) {\(e^-\)};
  \vertex (i2) at (-2,-1) {\(e^+\)};
  \vertex (a)  at (-0.6, 0);
  \vertex (b)  at ( 0.6, 0);
  \vertex (f1) at ( 2, 1) {\(\mu^-\)};
  \vertex (f2) at ( 2,-1) {\(\mu^+\)};
  \diagram* {
    (i1) -- [fermion] (a) -- [fermion] (i2),
    (a)  -- [photon, edge label=\(\gamma\)] (b),
    (f1) -- [anti fermion] (b) -- [anti fermion] (f2),
  };
\end{feynman}
\end{tikzpicture}
"""

with_theme(text_handler = handler) do
    fig = Figure(size = (760, 340))
    Label(fig[1, 1], diagram; fontsize = 16, tellheight = false)
    ax = Axis(fig[1, 2];
        title  = L"e^-e^+ \to \mu^-\mu^+ \text{ (tree level)}",
        xlabel = L"\cos\theta",
        ylabel = L"d\sigma/d\cos\theta",
    )
    θ = range(-1, 1; length = 200)
    lines!(ax, θ, 1 .+ θ.^2; label = L"\propto 1 + \cos^2\theta")
    axislegend(ax; position = :ct)
    fig
end
```

`render_strings = true` routes plain `String`s through LaTeX too, so tick labels and the legend match the math. Set it to `false` to keep plain strings on Makie's default FreeType path (much faster, but the two fonts won't match unless you align them yourself).

## Vector assets as scatter markers

`MakieTeX.PDF` and `MakieTeX.SVG` wrap a vector file for use as a scatter `marker`. CairoMakie renders them vector-natively (Poppler / librsvg); GLMakie / WGLMakie rasterize them at GPU-upload time:

```{julia}
julia_logo  = MakieTeX.SVG(joinpath(ASSETS, "julia_dots.svg"))
python_logo = MakieTeX.SVG(joinpath(ASSETS, "python.svg"))
matlab_logo = MakieTeX.SVG(joinpath(ASSETS, "matlab.svg"))

languages = ["Julia", "Python", "MATLAB"]
ages      = [14, 35, 42]                       # years since first release, 2026
logos     = [julia_logo, python_logo, matlab_logo]

fig = Figure(size = (640, 240))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1];
    title  = "Age of programming languages in 2026",
    xlabel = "years since first release",
    yticks = (1:length(languages), languages),
    limits = (0, 52, 0.4, length(languages) + 0.6),
    xgridvisible = false, ygridvisible = false,
    yticksvisible = false,
)
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)

barplot!(ax, 1:length(ages), ages;
    direction = :x, color = (:steelblue, 0.4), strokewidth = 0,
    bar_labels = ["$(a) years" for a in ages],
    label_offset = 8)

scatter!(ax, ages, 1:length(ages); marker = logos, markersize = 28,
    marker_offset = Vec2f(-20, 0))
fig
```

A scalar `markersize` sets the longer dimension and the shorter one scales to preserve the asset's aspect ratio — same convention as `Char` and `BezierPath` markers.
